department: Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, Clarence M. Mitchell, Jr. School of Engineering

deadline.value: School of Graduate Studies sets April 1 as the Fall application deadline for international F-1 degree-seeking applicants (unless an earlier program deadline applies); Morgan's Application Deadlines portal lists May 1, 2027 for Sustainable & Resilient Infrastructure Engineering, PhD (Fall 2027), and SGS funding applications are due April 30.
deadline.quote: Application deadlines for the School of Graduate Studies (SGS) are as follows (unless earlier deadline dates are indicated by the individual programs): ... International, degree-seeking (All F-1 in and out of USA) Fall - April 1

also.quote: Sustainable & Resilient Infrastructure Engineering, PhD Saturday, May 1, 2027 Fall 2027 Graduate Sustainable & Resilient Infrastructure Engineering, PhD

gre_subject.value: No GRE Subject Test exists for Civil & Environmental Engineering; ETS offers Subject Tests only in Mathematics, Physics, and Psychology.
gre_subject.quote: The GRE Subject Tests in Mathematics, Physics and Psychology measure undergraduate achievement in a particular field of study

supervisor.value: Students form a doctoral advisory committee by the end of the first or second year; no pre-admission advisor commitment is stated.

funding.value: Graduate assistantships (TA/RA, $21,000 doctoral stipend plus tuition award up to 9 credits/semester excluding university fees) and fellowships require a separate School of Graduate Studies funding application (due April 30 for Fall) and are not guaranteed.
funding.quote: SUBMISSION OF A FUNDING APPLICATION DOES NOT MEAN YOU WILL BE APPROVED. The decisions will be based on program selection and availability of funding per each program. | Graduate assistantships for doctoral and master's degree students pay a stipend ($21,000-doctoral $12,000-master's) Tuition awards do not pay for university and miscellaneous fees.

entry_route.value: Requires 60 graduate credit hours beyond a bachelor's degree (with pass-through en passant M.S. after 30 credits) or 36 graduate credit hours beyond a master's degree.
entry_route.quote: Complete a minimum of 36 graduate credit hours (including 15 hours of dissertation-related research) of study beyond the master’s degree or complete a minimum of 60 graduate credit hours (including 15 hours of dissertation-related research) of study beyond the bachelors’ degree.

notes: Morgan State's Department of Transportation and Urban Infrastructure Studies also offers a separate post-master's Ph.D. in Transportation and Urban Infrastructure Systems (36 credits, GRE required, April 1 international / May 1, 2027 Fall deadlines).
name: Sustainable and Resilient Infrastructure Engineering
